features.layout: x = [rmsnorm(emb) * emb_norm.weight, h_prev, h_lag]; h_lag absent for targets t < lag
features.emb: the embed_tokens row of the token (bf16 widened to f32)
features.h: the MoE block input (post_attention_layernorm output); h_prev at target t for the previous token (zero at position 0), h_lag at target t - lag for this token
features.output: z = lin.weight @ x + lin.bias [+ mlp.2.weight @ gelu(mlp.0.weight @ x + mlp.0.bias) + mlp.2.bias]; the top m of z name the experts of target t

training.data: wikitext-103, FineWeb-Edu, UltraChat, code, agent transcripts (hermes, openhands, swesmith); see results/router_training.json data_cfg
training.objective: KL(released softmax || router softmax) per layer

derived.for: memory-limited iPhones (the phone-small profile) only; tokens differ from the 8-bit set
derived.made_by: ms_derive resident DIR --bits 4 --from-calibrated FILE (calibrated 4-bit export, same tensors, size and layout as the plain set)
derived.quality: on the iPhone 15 Plus, top choice equal to the exact 8-bit engine on 0.913 / 0.884 of prose / agent-text positions in exact mode and 0.891 / 0.881 in fast (threshold 0.08), measured on the device; the plain set it replaces: 0.88 / 0.85 (Mac)

generated.by: moved-store release tools, from the manifest of 2026-11-21 plus the new parts

exact.definition: Generated tokens never depend on the cache, the routers or timing: the model's own router picks 8 experts per layer and the engine waits for every one.

fast.definition: The model's own router still picks. A picked expert that is not in memory is waited for if its routing weight is over 0.1 or its read is already in flight; otherwise it is left out (no substitute, no renormalisation). Router names are on.

calibration.measured: base M4 16 GB, 5.0 GB cache, mac profile, linear_k2 names, run-ahead on; the 35B's / Inkling's code prompt (357 / 462 tokens) then exact mode's own 650 tokens teacher-forced (650 positions), two alternating pairs, AC, other processes 200-400% CPU

rows.setting: weight 0.1, wait for reads in flight (this)

calibration.reason: kept: the one leave-out rule (fast-eps) measured worse on the iPhone (phone-small, where fast mode is the default: 3.57 against 4.1 tok/s); on the Mac it ran faster (14.9 against 13.1 tok/s in the clean run; the 6.38 run had 400% other CPU) at agreement 0.980 against 0.982

fast-eps.definition: Fast mode under the one leave-out rule (Flash-Next's and Inkling's fast mode): the picked experts that are not in memory are read, heaviest first, until those left weigh at most 0.13 of the step's routing weight; those are left out (no substitute, no renormalisation); a light pick whose read is in flight is not waited for. Selectable (--mode fast-eps), not this model's fast mode: measured worse on the iPhone (3.57 against 4.1 tok/s); on the Mac faster (see fast.calibration).

mac.cache_rule: locked; size chosen from free memory at start (ceiling = physical memory - 5.5 GB - the process's other memory); shrinks 1 GB per check under memory pressure and grows back
mac.bytes_rule: sum of the listed parts' bytes; moved-store.json is fetched first and is not listed

calibration.measured: base M4 16 GB, AC, the merged build (next), mac profile; 400 tokens after the model's code prompt, cache 6.6 GB; MB read per token, the published engine's beside
calibration.reason: off on the Mac: keeping the prompt apart from the decode's cache statistics (on from a Flash-Next measurement) cost this model decode reads after a long prompt, in exact and fast mode; the phone profiles keep the model-level value until measured on the iPhone

phone.when: iOS with at least 5.0 GB available at open
phone.cache_rule: locked slab sized at open: available - in-memory weights - router - 0.3 GB - 0.9 GB margin, clamped to 0.6-8 GB
phone.bytes_rule: sum of the listed parts' bytes; moved-store.json is fetched first and is not listed

calibration.measured: iPhone 15 Plus (A16), phone-small, exact, 4 prefill threads, the cold 472-token input at a 1.42 GB slab (results/ios/p2/P2.md, 2026-11-23): first token 19.5 s at 0.65 / 0.65 against 24.6 s without the split (21.5-25.2 s, Nov 22) and 22.3 s at 0.5 / 0.5; reply ids identical (60 of 60); footprint peak 3.44 GB in the prefill, 2.73 GB in the decode after it
calibration.reason: the GPU split pays on this phone for this model
calibration.carried: measured on the 6 GB iPhone 15 Plus (phone-small) and carried to phone: the cause is iOS's shared CPU / GPU power budget, not the memory class; the app has passed this share on phone so far, so the resolved behaviour on phones does not change

phone-small.when: iOS with less than 5.0 GB available at open (the 6 GB class)

fast.definition: the model-level fast mode with the leave-out threshold of this profile's calibrated 4-bit in-memory weights: a picked expert not in memory is waited for if its routing weight is over 0.08 or its read is in flight, otherwise left out

calibration.measured: top choice equal to the exact 8-bit engine, prose / agent text, the calibrated 4-bit in-memory weights (engine session, Mac): 0.900 / 0.885 at threshold 0.08, 0.888 / 0.878 at 0.09, 0.860 / 0.873 at 0.10 (the model-level value); exact 0.913 / 0.884; on the iPhone 15 Plus (phone-small, 1.42 GB slab, 400 tokens of prose) 3.52 tok/s at 0.08 (results/ios/p2/P2.md)
calibration.reason: 0.10 gives up 0.04 of prose agreement on these weights; 0.08 keeps fast within 0.013 of exact; the 8-bit profiles keep the model-level threshold

calibration.measured: iPhone 15 Plus, phone-small, fast at threshold 0.08 with linear_k2, 8 readers, slab 1.485 GB, 200 tokens each, one run per cell, judged by counters (results/ios/p2/P2.md, names at threshold 0.08, 2026-11-23): plain top 3 4.33 tok/s, wait / compute 157 / 74 ms, 153 MB per token; the confidence rule (tau 0.5 over 16) 3.94 tok/s, 183 / 70 ms, 167 MB; plain top 2 4.06 tok/s; no names 3.92 tok/s
calibration.reason: fast: a plain top 3, the lowest wait; exact: the confidence rule, as every profile; the app set this pair before it was declared here; the confidence rule in fast is to be measured again on the phone for the 35B once its restore is in (staged 2026-11-26)

phone-small.cache_rule: locked slab sized at open by cache_slab: the 2.96 GB app footprint target of the 6 GB class less this model's footprint beside the cache, clamped to 0.6-8 GB

calibration.measured: iPhone 15 Plus (6 GB), phone-small, flash-last / release builds, 2026-11-26: the app footprint beside the expert cache in decode, 1.54 GB (4-bit in-memory weights, router, state, checkpoints); footprint 2.93-2.95 GB in decode at the 1.42 GB slab (results/ios/p2/P2.md)
calibration.reason: sized for an app footprint of 2.96 GB on the 6 GB class (the old app's footprint on this phone, the equal-footprint comparison of results/ios/p2/P2.md) instead of from the memory iOS reports at open; the target belongs to the device class, the non-cache footprint to the model: 2.96 - 1.54 = 1.42 GB

phone-small.status: top choice equal to the exact 8-bit engine, prose / agent text, measured on the iPhone 15 Plus: exact 0.913 / 0.884, fast (threshold 0.08) 0.891 / 0.881
phone-small.bytes_rule: sum of the listed parts' bytes; moved-store.json is fetched first and is not listed

calibration.measured: iPhone 15 Plus (A16), phone-small, exact, 4 prefill threads, the cold 472-token input at a 1.42 GB slab (results/ios/p2/P2.md, 2026-11-23): first token 19.5 s at 0.65 / 0.65 against 24.6 s without the split (21.5-25.2 s, Nov 22) and 22.3 s at 0.5 / 0.5; reply ids identical (60 of 60); footprint peak 3.44 GB in the prefill, 2.73 GB in the decode after it
calibration.reason: the GPU split pays on this phone for this model

calibration.measured: iPhone 15 Plus, phone-small, 2026-11-26: the state's KV reserve at 16,384 positions is 0.336 GB, inside the 1.54 GB non-cache footprint (cache_slab)
calibration.reason: the positions every front end reserves on this profile: the value the app set

notes.routers: linear_k2 names experts 2 layers early; its engine file is derived/router.linear_k2.q8...bin
notes.names: the confidence rule (tau 0.5 of 16 candidates) on every profile, as Inkling: measured on the base M4 (5.0 GB cache, exact, the code prompt and 200 tokens, two alternating pairs, AC, other processes 200-400% CPU): 128.5 / 128.7 MB per token, 8.14 / 13.23 tok/s, wait 11.9 / 13.8 ms against a top 8 143.4 / 143.5 MB, 9.13 / 11.16 tok/s, 14.7 / 13.9 ms: 10% fewer bytes, speed within the runs' spread
notes.prompt_path: batched span prefill, prefix cache with disk checkpoints, idle-time prefill of the next turn, saved hot set
notes.priority_reads: speculative reads (router and cross-token names) by priority, nearest step first, instead of first in, first out: the same for every family

layout.rule: engine-ready files are in derived/ under the engine's own names (<id>.<engine_format>.<first 12 hex of the source part's sha256>.bin); the engine looks for them in DIR/derived/ as well as DIR/.dmeng/ and derives what is missing into DIR/.dmeng/
layout.profile_rule: the engine picks the profile from the device; --profile NAME overrides it, --mode exact|fast overrides the profile's mode

prefill.notes: the batched prompt path (dmeng/prefill.h): sub-chunk, span, names of the next layer (whole from 1000 positions, else its released router's picks), the last span joined under 64 positions, the GPU's share from sub-chunks of 64 (as Flash-Next; measured on a base M4 before the shared prompt path: 192-token prompts 6.0 -> 4.3 s for the 35B, 9.7 -> 8.3 s for Inkling against 256), the experts in waves as they land (a wave on the GPU from 128 rows), every expert and the shared expert through the packed kernels, down projections in 64-row jobs: the values this model's prefill was written and measured with (results/ios/p3-gpu/GPU-PREFILL.md); the prompt's memory as every family's (prompt_plan): a scratch bound of 768 MB (scratch_mb: the sub-chunk at most a quarter, the span the rest, equal spans) and the transient buffers lent by the cache with prefill_release (lend), as Flash-Next; the prompt kept apart from the decode's cache statistics (apart, the hazard policy only: placement), as Flash-Next; fast mode: a prompt of at most 64 positions keeps the decode's leave-out rule in its batched pass (drop_upto 64, the value Flash-Next declares, the old runner's threshold), longer prompts lossless

cost_prior.measured: base M4, dmeng step costs of passes of 1-8 positions (the drafting controller's prior as on main; a draft_cost.txt measured by the engine replaces it)

cost_prior_alternative.estimated: not used by the engine: from the measured parts of the verify pass after its fixes (the recurrent state streamed once per pass, the screened head, the packed gemm from 2 positions): 1.15 at 2 positions and 2.8 at 8, linear between; to replace the measured prior only after a real-model measurement

drafting.default_note:
profiles.

.drafts = {lookup, head}: drafting by default (lookup: the lookup and tool-call drafts; head: none (this family has no draft head: a profile declaring head fails at open)), resolved once for dmeng, dmserve and the C API (which has no drafting: a declared default stays off there, an explicit request is refused); --drafts 0|1 and --draft none|lookup|fixed|head|both override it; off on every profile until measured on the real model
